name: Engram against a plain .md memory file on LongMemEval, rule fixed on 7 November 2026 before any .md answer exists
question: Does Engram's tested search help a small model more than the simple memory everyday chat apps use: notes written after each conversation, read back as one file?
data: xiaowu0162/longmemeval-cleaned, longmemeval_s_cleaned.json (MIT licence); the same 470 test questions and split as frozen_design_lme.json
engram: the recorded answers of 'networks without facts' in results/lme_answers.jsonl (47.4% in the earlier marking); nothing in Engram is run, tuned or changed
md_memory: after each conversation Gemma 3 4B (the same model and file) writes a note of at most 40 words with the NOTE prompt in kit_tools/md_test.py; the notes, dated, oldest first, NONE left out, form the file
answer: the same Gemma, the same answer prompt as Engram (checked against vps_kit.py), the question with today's date, 60 reply tokens, temperature 0

systems.md_full: the whole file; if over 3,000 tokens, the oldest notes are dropped until it fits the model's 4,096-token window
systems.md_equal: the latest notes within the same number of tokens Engram gave the model for that question (816 on average)

how_many_questions: the first test questions in hash order whose sessions can be noted within 5 hours at the speed measured on 24 development sessions; at least 100; fixed in md_plan.json before any test note is written
score: blind labels by Claude agents with LongMemEval's per-type rules (kit_tools/lme_rules.md); Engram's answers on the same questions are marked again in the same mixed batches with system names hidden, so both arms are judged the same way; agreement with the earlier marks is reported
primary_measure: Engram minus md_full, same questions, 95% interval by paired bootstrap

reading.interval above zero: Engram helps the small model more than a .md memory file
reading.interval below zero: a .md memory file helps more than Engram
reading.interval across zero: no difference shown; Engram's extra machinery is not justified by this test

secondary: Engram minus md_equal (same amount of text); by question type; not-answerable questions; text given
limits_stated_now: these questions were used once before for Engram, though nothing was tuned on them; one model; a note-per-chat file is one common kind of .md memory, not every product's; Claude marks the answers, not LongMemEval's GPT-4o judge
allowed_to_fail: the result is reported whichever way it goes, and neither arm is changed and rerun on these questions
